title: Zoom in: building one inbox page
caption: Pushed entries are already in the user's list; the read only adds the few popular repos they watch, then hydrates and filters the page.

steps.text: Read the user's inbox list: event ids pushed by the fan-out workers, newest first.
From the user's watch list, keep only the repos above the threshold. Usually that is zero to a few.
Fetch the recent events of those repos from the replicated recents, in parallel, with a short timeout.
Merge both lists by time and drop repeats by event id (an event can be pushed and merged if the threshold changed).
Hydrate the page's ids into titles and authors in one batch, drop anything deleted or no longer visible, and return the page.

scenarios.name: Returning user
scenarios.summary: Someone opens the inbox after a year away. Their list was evicted to save memory, so it is rebuilt once by pulling.

steps.text: No inbox list is found: inactive users' lists are evicted.
Pull recent events from each watched repo, merge them and store the result as the new list. This one open is slow.
From here the normal path runs, and later opens are fast again.

scenarios.name: Recents fetch times out
scenarios.summary: One popular repo's recents don't answer in time. The page is served without them instead of failing.

steps.text: The fetch for one popular repo misses its 50 ms timeout.
Skip that repo and mark the page partial; the client can refresh in a moment.
The pushed entries and the other repos still make a full page.

scenarios.name: Repo made private
scenarios.summary: The owner makes a repo private after its events were pushed. Copies stay in inboxes, so access is checked at hydration, not at fan-out.

steps.text: The list still holds event ids from the repo that is now private.
Hydration checks the reader's access for each event's repo and drops the ones they can no longer see.
The page is a little shorter, and nothing leaks. Capped lists age the stale ids out on their own.
